correctness.rationale: The local E/N swap cannot cross forbidden equality at any fault layer. A fixed fault-side assignment imposes order-ideal or order-filter inequalities whose meet/join-closed order-convex intersection is a distributive lattice interval; its toggles realize symmetric-difference shortest paths and the median metric. A pair of independent four-step choices per diagonal fault realizes all 2^k signatures; primitive excursions and the even Catalan generating function prove the C_{2k} total. The included independent exhaustive/DP verifiers pass 918 finite grid cases and k up to 12 respectively; infinite conclusions use the written proofs.

value.rationale: Robust reconfiguration under multiple node failures is a natural route-control problem. Despite exponentially many surviving optimal routes, k faults can create the maximum 2^k mutually unreachable optimal-route islands. The theorem determines every component and exact distances on arbitrary rectangular grids and explains a surprising Catalan survivor law for the sharp extremizers, yielding a reusable structural network-rerouting benchmark distinct from a trivial finite tabulation.
